scLabel.value: Shortage of people to carry on the work

sLabel.value: Shortage of people to carry on the work

oLabel.value: A significant decline in the working-age population

opText.value: It is considered inevitable that a sharp decline in the working-age population will cause a shortage of people to carry on local industries

tText.value: A particularly serious challenge is the sharp decline in the working-age population, those aged 15 to 64. In 1980, 43 years ago, there were about 84,600 working-age people; 20 years later, in 2000, there were about 75,500, a decrease of about 9,000 over two decades. By 2020, the figure had fallen to about 53,700, meaning that in the 20 years since the start of the 21st century, the working-age population declined by about 22,000. In a city of roughly 100,000 people, losing about 22,000 working-age residents in 20 years naturally leads to labor shortages in every field.

oLabel.value: Changes in social structure since the system was established

stLabel.value: Head of the Health and Welfare Division Nakagawa

opText.value: Unlike the era centered on agriculture, forestry, and fisheries, the asset-based levy no longer reflects reality

tText.value: When the National Health Insurance system was established in the 1950s, many enrollees were farmers, forestry and fishery workers, or self-employed people. The asset-based component was introduced to supplement the income-based component under the ability-to-pay principle. Today, pensioners and unemployed people make up much of the enrollment, and their assets are often homes they live in. It is questionable whether taxing such assets through the asset-based component is appropriate; it no longer reflects actual circumstances.

tText.value: The construction defect we have referred to is what is known in construction terminology as honeycombing.
